question: Nirmal invests a sum of ₹5400 and Rakesh invests a sum of ₹9400 at the same rate of simple interest per annum. If, at the end of 5 years, Rakesh gets ₹360 more interest than Nirmal, then find the rate of interest per annum (in percentage).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference in principal = ₹9400 − ₹5400 = ₹4000

Extra interest earned on this difference in 5 years = ₹360

Extra interest per year = 360 ÷ 5 = ₹72

Rate of interest = (72 ÷ 4000) × 100 = 1.8%

**∴ The correct answer is 1.8%.**
